# Statistics for Data Science

## Chapter 1 — Descriptive statistics
Mean, median and mode describe the centre of a distribution. Variance and standard deviation describe its spread. The median is robust to outliers, the mean is not. Always plot the data (histogram, box plot) before computing summary numbers.

## Chapter 2 — Probability distributions
A random variable maps outcomes to numbers. Key distributions: Bernoulli (one trial), Binomial (n trials), Poisson (counts per interval), Normal (sums of many small effects, central limit theorem). The Normal distribution is defined by its mean and standard deviation.

## Chapter 3 — Hypothesis testing
State H0 and H1, choose a significance level (often 5%), compute a test statistic and its p-value. A p-value below the level leads to rejecting H0. A non-significant result does not prove H0. Common tests: t-test (means), chi-square (categories).

## Chapter 4 — Linear regression
Linear regression models y as a linear function of features. Coefficients are estimated by least squares. Check residuals for patterns, R² for explained variance, and beware of multicollinearity and extrapolation.
